opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Black (employee ID E008) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E008.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Black (E008) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. She requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted. As a full-time employee, maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E008 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Karen requested admin to Source Code, but her max is read. HR note claimed full-time, but Security DB record shows contractor. Recommend read.
reason: Karen Black (E008) requested admin access to Source Code. The Security DB record identifies her as a contractor with basic security training, so per policy contractors max out at read (write would require advanced training) and admin is never permitted. Even under the HR note's full-time classification, admin would not be allowed because Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist, capping at write. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read for a contractor with basic training), the granted level is the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Karen Black (E008)
Request: admin access to Source Code

Two notes:
- HR note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommends write (max write for full-time, admin only if role owns system; Source Code owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist).
- Security note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read. Contractors: read, or write only with advanced training. Never admin. Security DB shows contractor.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor.

The Approver reads the notes and makes final decision. Which source to trust? Typically security DB is authoritative for security-related facts. The security note explicitly states HR note claimed full-time but Security DB record shows contractor.

Access policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Karen has basic training, so max is read.

Requested level: admin, which is above max. Grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit.
